task: Help me turn this into a firm but polite claim summary for my insurer that explains who was at fault and what I'm asking them to cover.
text:
Subject: claim for rear-end collision, policy MTR-55-208-417

Hello, I'm writing about the accident on 14 September at roughly 17:40 on the ring road roundabout. The other driver, Kaveh Rostami, drove into the back of my car while I was stopped at the give-way line; he admitted at the scene that he was looking at his phone. His insurer's reference is 88-QX-30917. My rear bumper and the parking sensors were damaged, and the garage quoted 1,860 euros, not including the hire car. A witness, Ilse Vermeulen, said she'd confirm what she saw, though she only saw the impact, not the moment before. Ilse's statement isn't written yet. Please send any forms to 12 Kestrel Row, Lindmouth LM4 7QT, not to my old address. My excess is 300 euros.

decisions.label: ACCOUNT_ID
decisions.reason: The policy number links the claim to the policyholder; the summary only needs to reference it, so exact verification is lost and the user re-adds it when sending.

decisions.label: ACCOUNT_ID
decisions.reason: The third party's insurer reference identifies another policyholder and is not needed to explain fault or costs.

decisions.label: ADDRESS
decisions.reason: The home address identifies the claimant; the summary only needs to say forms should go to the current address.

The other driver,
drove into the back of my car while I was stopped at the give-way line; he admitted at the scene that he was looking at his phone.
My rear bumper and the parking sensors were damaged, and the garage quoted 1,860 euros, not including the hire car.
A witness,

approved_output:
Subject: claim for rear-end collision, policy [ACCOUNT_ID]

Hello, I'm writing about the accident on 14 September at roughly 17:40 on the ring road roundabout. The other driver, [PERSON_1], drove into the back of my car while I was stopped at the give-way line; he admitted at the scene that he was looking at his phone. His insurer's reference is [ACCOUNT_ID]. My rear bumper and the parking sensors were damaged, and the garage quoted 1,860 euros, not including the hire car. A witness, [PERSON_2], said she'd confirm what she saw, though she only saw the impact, not the moment before. [PERSON_2]'s statement isn't written yet. Please send any forms to [ADDRESS], not to my old address. My excess is 300 euros.

review.notes: BLOCKING FACT_COVERAGE (ruling 17): two values render as the same [ACCOUNT_ID] ('Subject: claim for rear-end collision, policy [ACCOUNT_ID]' and 'His insurer's reference is [ACCOUNT_ID].'). The writer marks the own policy number essential ('the summary only needs to reference it') and the notes say 'surrounding role words keep them distinguishable', so the claim summary must keep them apart, yet neither distinguishing phrase is required: 'claim for rear-end collision, policy' and 'His insurer's reference is' are both outside required_facts. Minimal repair: add required quotes 'claim for rear-end collision, policy' (or at least 'policy') and 'His insurer's reference is'. Otherwise good: 'Kaveh Rostami' -> [PERSON_1]; 'Ilse Vermeulen'/'Ilse' -> [PERSON_2]; address -> [ADDRESS]; fault, 1,860 euros excluding hire car, witness hedge 'only saw the impact, not the moment before' and 300-euro excess survive. NOTE: 'Please send any forms to' + ', not to my old address.' is not required; not a task dependency, but cheap to add. NOTE: the other insurer's reference is arguably essential too (the claim lets the insurer pursue the third party); ruling 1 allows either.

task: Work out how much I still owe my brother, by when, and what changes if I'm late, so I can message him.
text: Can you help me get this straight before I message my brother? Last spring my brother, Emeka Obi, lent me 2,000 euros for the car repair. Correction to what I told you yesterday: I've repaid 1,200 of it, not 1,400. The 200 I sent in July went to his partner, Chiamaka, for the concert tickets, not toward the loan. Emeka said I don't owe any interest, but only if the rest is cleared by the end of December; after that he wants 3% on whatever is left. Separately, my friend Lior Ben-David owes me 150 euros, and he thinks he might be able to pay it in two halves, maybe 75 in November and 75 in January. Until Lior actually pays, I'm not counting that money towards what I owe my brother.

review.notes: BLOCKING FACT_COMPLETENESS (ruling 15, condition): the source claim 'Until Lior actually pays, I'm not counting that money towards what I owe my brother.' is required only as "actually pays, I'm not counting that money towards what I owe my brother." With the alias, the required quotes read '[PERSON_3] actually pays, I'm not counting that money...'. Losing 'Until' drops the condition and turns a temporary exclusion into a flat statement, and that condition decides whether the friend's 150 euros can offset the debt the task asks about. Minimal repair: add 'Until' as its own required fragment (it occurs once). Otherwise strong: 'Emeka Obi'/'Emeka', 'Chiamaka', 'Lior Ben-David'/'Lior' aliased distinctly; the loan, the 1,200-not-1,400 correction, the 200 to the partner 'not toward the loan', the interest-free-only-if-cleared-by-December condition with 3% after, and the friend's hedged repayment are required. 132 words, preservation/consumer fits.
